bike.summary: Hourly bike rentals are successfully predicted using multiple features from the dataset, achieving a test RMSE of 99.2 rentals compared to a mean baseline of 168.6 rentals and an R-squared of 0.65. The best cross-validated results are achieved using 35 features, and including all 37 available features yields a very similar test RMSE of 99.3. The models comfortably outperform the random subsets median cross-validated RMSE of 108.4.
findings: The best overall configuration uses Lasso feature selection with an ElasticNet model at k equals 35, yielding a test RMSE of 99.2 and an R-squared of 0.65.
Different feature selection methods achieve nearly identical cross-validated RMSE values around 106.1.
The strongest positive standardized effect on rentals is observed for hour 18 with an effect size of 73.9, followed closely by hour 17 at 70.6.
Hour 8 also shows a strong positive effect of 59.3, while temperature increases rentals with an effect size of 44.2.
bike.recommendation: Use Lasso feature selection with an ElasticNet model at k equals 35 because it achieves the best test RMSE and R-squared while slightly reducing model complexity.
caveats: The evaluation is based on a held-out test set of 400 rows, sampled from a larger dataset of 2,000 total rows.
Columns representing row identifiers, dates, and direct components of the target variable like casual and registered counts were dropped to prevent data leakage.
Regression coefficients indicate statistical associations and do not necessarily imply direct causation.

kc.summary: Multiple linear regression models were trained to predict house prices in King County using a dataset of 2,000 properties. The best model achieved a test RMSE of 183,540 US dollars and an R-squared of 0.74, substantially outperforming the mean baseline RMSE of 357,147 US dollars. Models using larger feature subsets generally improved performance, with the optimal feature count reaching 35 to 37 features.
findings: The best overall cross-validated result was achieved using the Lasso feature selection method with an ElasticNet model at k equals 35 features, yielding a cross-validated RMSE of 190,889 US dollars.
F-test, MI, and RFE methods all achieved their best performance using Ridge regression with 37 features, resulting in a test RMSE of 183,211 US dollars and an R-squared of 0.74.
Interior living space showed the strongest positive standardized effect, increasing price by 134,229 US dollars per standard deviation.
Construction and design quality also strongly increased price, adding 114,964 US dollars per standard deviation.
Being located in an unlisted zipcode had a strong negative effect, decreasing price by 66,497 US dollars relative to the reference zipcode.
kc.recommendation: It is recommended to use the Ridge model with features selected via F-test, MI, or RFE at k equals 37, as this configuration achieved the best test RMSE of 183,211 US dollars and highest R-squared of 0.74.
caveats: Evaluations were performed on a held-out test set of 400 rows, sampled from a larger population of 21,613 properties.
Redundant columns such as identifiers and linear combinations like sqft_above were dropped during data preparation.
Observed relationships reflect statistical associations and do not necessarily imply direct causation.
